key_insight: Raising argon flow from 1600 to 1800 L/h during air plasma spraying made NiCrFeBSiC coatings thicker, denser, and more wear-resistant.
engineering_relevance: For thermal-spray process tuning, argon flow is a practical control knob to improve coating integrity and tribological performance without changing the alloy system.
method: Air plasma sprayed self-fluxing NiCrFeBSiC metal-ceramic coatings at two argon flow rates: 1600 and 1800 L/h.
Compared microstructure, porosity, thickness, microhardness, elastic modulus, friction, and adhesion.
Used ball-on-disk tribology and scratch testing to assess wear and coating-substrate bonding.
evidence_signal: The higher argon flow approximately doubled coating thickness and halved porosity, while lowering the friction coefficient to about 0.107 and maintaining high adhesion with similar critical loads.
watch_item: Results are based on only two argon flow settings, so broader process optimization and long-term durability should be verified before scale-up.
paper_title: EFFECT OF ARGON FLOW RATE DURING AIR PLASMA SPRAYING ON THE STRUCTURE AND PROPERTIES OF NICRFEBSIC COATINGS
